chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Verily, maintaining ties of kinship and righteousness ease the Reckoning and protect from sins. So maintain ties with your relatives and be righteous with your brethren, even if it is through good greeting and responding to it.'
ai.seo_question: How does maintaining family ties affect one's judgment in the afterlife according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links silat al-rahim (maintaining kinship ties) and birr (righteousness) as dual mechanisms that alleviate the severity of the Day of Judgment and provide protection from sins. He emphasizes the accessibility of this virtue, noting that even minimal gestures like exchanging good greetings (hussn al-salam) suffice, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on the practical, everyday nature of spiritual purification through social bonds.
